trust_decision.summary: Whether the OPA policy is told that the request body it sees was truncated at max-request-body-size. Skipper reads the body in ExtractHttpBodyOptionally/fillBuffer, then builds the ext_authz CheckRequest in AdaptToExtAuthRequest. When the request has no Content-Length (chunked or HTTP/2), nothing marks the body as truncated, so input.truncated_body stays false and the policy sees a partial body as a complete one.

landing_point.why: The earlier chunked/HTTP-2 fix (GHSA-8qqm, the expectedSize=-1 handling at :1320-1329) and the truncation comment at :1340-1344 are here. An engineer reading 'truncated_body fails open on chunked/HTTP-2' starts at ExtractHttpBodyOptionally/fillBuffer.

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The advisory is about body authorization (allow/deny), and the docs say opaServeResponse 'has no real allow/deny' (docs/reference/filters.md:2354-2356). A solver could leave opaServeResponseWithReqBody alone as a response-serving feature, not an authz gate. But if the solver changes the ExtractHttpBodyOptionally signature, the Go compiler forces them to update this caller anyway.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Legitimate chunked/HTTP-2 bodies that fit under max-request-body-size (and bodies with Content-Length within the limit) must still reach the policy with truncated_body=false. Rejecting every request without Content-Length, or flagging every body whose length equals the cap, would break these. The SkipRequestBodyParse path (body not read) must keep passing a nil body and must not be flagged.
